item.title: Liverpool wonderkid to be given golden chance by Andoni Iraola
item.description: Liverpool's starting XI has already been changed multiple times this season. Andoni Iraola is yet to find his strongest 11 thanks to the sheer number of injuries his team have suffered.Of course, some...
item.content:encoded:
Liverpool's starting XI has already been changed multiple times this season.

Andoni Iraola is yet to find his strongest 11 thanks to the sheer number of injuries his team have suffered.

Of course, some members of his squad have managed to nail their positions down such as Ronald Araujo, Alisson and Virgil van Dijk but others, mainly in their attack, still haven't managed to do that yet.

From an outsiders perspective, this could mean one of two things, the first being that they have too many good players among their ranks and can't decide with the second being that they don't have enough talent.

Obviously, it's unclear which way Iraola feels about his squad but, the fact that one of Liverpool's wonderkids could be about to get handed a golden opportunity by the Spaniard means that he's happy to experiment and figure out who his best options are.

Trey Nyoni could be handed a starting role now that Dominik Szoboszlai is out injured again

Since Trey Nyoni is only be 19 years old, he's seen as one of Liverpool's brightest prospects.

Most fans thought that the Englishman would get loaned out this term with clubs such as Swansea showing an interest in him.

However, after Arne Slot was sacked, it was clear that wasn't going to be the case as he stopped him from exiting thanks to his pre-season performances.

Since then, he's played a fairly regular role for Liverpool but, now that Dominik Szoboszlai is injured, he may have more of a chance at starting for the Reds.

When he's been used alongside Alexis Mac Allister in the middle of the park, the duo have formed a dynamic partnership and have often won most of the midfield battles that they've faced.

This is majorly different to how things pan out with Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch who seem to make one another worse when used as a double pivot.

Obviously, changes could be made to try and resolve this but, with the Hungarian out of action, now feels like the time for Nyoni to shine.

Trey Nyoni could be Liverpool's next Fabinho

One player that Liverpool have never managed to replace is Fabinho.

The Brazilian exited Anfield back in 2023 and, when he eft, most fans thought that someone would be signed in his place or an academy graduate such as Stefan Bajcetic would fill the void.

Obviously, none of these things ever happened which resulted in Mac Allister and Gravenberch filling in as the Reds' number six and, while they both did well, it was clear that neither of them were naturals in that position.

Nothing has proven that more than Gravenberch this season.

The Dutchman has barely had an impact on any of the games he's featured in with most fans asking him to be axed for Nyoni or Mac Allister.

As mentioned, Nyoni is only 19 years old so he obviously can't play two 90 minute games per week but, if he manages to do well in Szoboszlai's absence, he could make a solid name for himself in L4.

item.title: Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany expected to be ready for Arsenal
item.description: FC Bayern could have its leader back to face Arsenal.
item.content:encoded:
Good news for Bayern Munich ahead of tonight’s Champions League showdown with Arsenal — Vincent Kompany appears set to return to the dugout after battling a viral infection and hip issues.

According to a report from Bild (as captured by @iMiaSanMia), Kompany was on the pitch for Bayern’s pre-match activation session at Säbener Straße on Wednesday morning, confirming that he will be available for the crucial clash at the Allianz Arena.

The Belgian coach had missed both Monday’s training session and Tuesday’s preparations, with assistant coach Aaron Danks taking charge of the squad and handling media duties in his absence. There had been genuine uncertainty about whether Kompany would recover in time, particularly after reports of additional hip discomfort and physical weakness caused by his illness.

His return provides Bayern Munich with a welcome boost ahead of one of their biggest tests of the Champions League campaign. Kompany’s tactical preparation, touchline leadership, and ability to make adjustments during a match could prove particularly important against an Arsenal side that will demand concentration and discipline for the full 90 minutes.

Bayern Munich will still need to deliver on the pitch, but having their head coach back involved is an encouraging development. Now, the focus shifts to executing the game plan and securing a statement result against the Premier League opposition.

item.title: AC Milan wants to beat Juventus to sign Bundesliga star
item.description: Juventus are interested in signing Kim Min-jae and reuniting him with Luciano Spalletti following their successful time together at Napoli. The Bianconeri believe the Bayern Munich defender could stre...
item.content:encoded:
Juventus are interested in signing Kim Min-jae and reuniting him with Luciano Spalletti following their successful time together at Napoli. The Bianconeri believe the Bayern Munich defender could strengthen their squad, particularly if the German club becomes willing to consider offers for his signature.

Min-jae continues to receive playing time under Vincent Kompany in Bavaria, but his involvement does not rule out a potential departure if an attractive offer arrives. Juventus are monitoring the situation as they look for opportunities to improve their defensive options.

Juventus hope to reunite Min-jae with Spalletti

Juventus view Min-jae as a strong candidate to strengthen their team, with his previous relationship with Spalletti potentially giving them an advantage. The defender already understands the manager’s expectations, having worked with him during their successful spell at Napoli.

Spalletti would reportedly welcome the reunion as he looks to bring Juventus closer to the level he achieved with Napoli. Min-jae could offer qualities familiar to the manager and help him implement his preferred approach with the Bianconeri.

However, Juventus must first establish whether Bayern are prepared to negotiate a deal. Although the defender is reportedly available if the right offer emerges, his regular involvement under Kompany means a transfer cannot be taken for granted.

(Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images)

AC Milan join the race for the defender

According to Tuttojuve, AC Milan are also interested in signing Min-jae, potentially setting up competition between the two Italian clubs. Both sides could pursue the defender if Bayern become open to letting him leave.

Juventus may hope that his previous connection with Spalletti will help persuade him to move to Turin. Having already worked together, the pair would have an established understanding that could make the transition easier.

Nevertheless, that relationship does not guarantee Min-jae will choose Juventus. The defender will need to consider his own ambitions, his role at Bayern and the opportunities available to him elsewhere.

The Bianconeri must therefore be ready to compete for his signature and present a convincing proposal if they want to bring him back to Italy. Milan’s reported interest could make that task more difficult, particularly if both clubs decide to pursue a deal.

For now, Juventus will continue to monitor the situation as they consider their options. A reunion with Spalletti remains a possibility, but much will depend on Bayern’s willingness to sell and Min Jae’s decision about his future.

item.title: Arsenal manager makes striking confession ahead of Munich match
item.description: Arsenal return to Champions League action against Bayern Munich tonight, with Arteta making clear that last season’s near miss remains a powerful source of motivation.Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Im...
item.content:encoded:
Arsenal return to Champions League action against Bayern Munich tonight, with Arteta making clear that last season’s near miss remains a powerful source of motivation.

Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images

Mikel Arteta has admitted he is still not over Arsenal’s Champions League final defeat, with the manager saying the pain of coming so close continues to drive him as his side prepare to face Bayern Munich tonight.

Arsenal are attempting to go one better in Europe this season after missing out on the trophy in the final, and Arteta made clear ahead of the 8pm BST kick-off at the Allianz Arena that the disappointment has not faded.

Asked whether he had used the summer to get over the defeat, Arteta said: “I tried, but I haven’t managed!

“So I tried for many weeks in the summer, even today. And when I see the ball, when I see the music, when I see the scenes, I want it so badly.

“We know that we have to go step by step, but I think that fire is within the team and all of us individually because we know what we have to go through. By a penalty we were not champions of Europe, so let’s try again.”

That desire will be tested in Munich against a Bayern side who warmed up for Arsenal’s visit by demolishing RB Leipzig 6-1, with Luis Diaz scoring a hat-trick.

Arsenal’s weekend was rather less comfortable.

Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images

Noni Madueke’s deflected winner was secured a late victory away to Nottingham Forest, where Arteta’s side struggled to reproduce the attacking sharpness they had shown in their 3-0 win over Lille.

Bayern will not be at full strength. Michael Olise is suspended and Jamal Musiala remains injured, while Manuel Neuer has only recently returned to training after a foot problem and is still a doubt. Joshua Kimmich will also be absent due to a death in his family.

There are other reasons for Arsenal to travel with confidence. Bayern’s emphatic win over Leipzig followed successive draws against Augsburg and Viking, evidence that they can be frustrated. They have kept only three cleansheets this season, conceding nine goals eight games.
